claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates enhance high-temperature plastic strain in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitates enhance high-temperature toughness in tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
The untreated tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy is single-phase or minimally precipitated and lacks significant coherent nanoprecipitates.
A controlled heat treatment can induce stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation in the alloy.
The nanoprecipitation-inducing treatment produces uniformly dispersed coherent interfaces within the matrix.
Tensile testing at approximately 800°C represents conditions relevant to fusion plasma-facing components.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent nanoprecipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations.
Stress concentrations in the alloy can cause premature crack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates promote smoother dislocation glide.
Coherent nanoprecipitates minimize crack propagation during high-temperature deformation.
Treated samples will have greater high-temperature tensile ductility than an untreated baseline.
Treated samples will have greater high-temperature toughness than an untreated baseline.
The untreated baseline is expected to have lower high-temperature ductility and toughness because it lacks engineered coherent nanoprecipitates.
The mechanism should operate only when temperature is high enough to activate dislocation glide.
The mechanism depends on reliable control of precipitate volume fraction and coherence.
The mechanism may extend from tungsten-based alloys to similar refractory high-entropy alloys.
A tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy using this nanoprecipitation strategy achieved 2.15 GPa strength and 15% tensile ductility at ambient temperature and 1.05 GPa yield strength at 800°C.
The controlled comparison will use treated and untreated samples of the tungsten refractory high-entropy alloy and verify nanoprecipitate presence and coherence by TEM.

Failure to obtain statistically significant improvements in both ductility and toughness, or failure to associate nanoprecipitates with fewer stress concentrations and crack-initiation sites, would falsify the hypothesis.
